To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NK cells are educated through inhibitory receptor engagement with self MHC class I.
NK cell education is a process of functional maturation that is dependent on the presence of self-MHC class-I molecules.

NK cell education involves licensing by self-MHC I molecules through the NK cell inhibitory receptors, and that this licensing process is required for NK cell activation through NK cell activating receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel strategies to improve NK cell-based immunotherapy.
understanding the mechanisms that guide the education of NK cells, which is a fundamental process that enables NK cells to discriminate self from nonself.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that regulate NK cell development, function and education in health and disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MHC-dependent NK cell education is a complex process that is regulated in a tissue-dependent manner.
NK cells, like B cells and T cells, are educated by self-MHC.
NK cells are licensed to kill by self-MHC I molecules and that this education process is a prerequisite for NK cell activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MHC class I expression on hematopoietic cells and NK cells is critical for NK cell functional maturation and competence, which is achieved by a process of MHC class I-dependent licensing of NK cell function.

NK cell education, which is the process by which NK cells acquire their functional competence, is a dynamic process that is regulated by the expression of self-MHC class-I molecules on the target cell surface.

NK cells are licensed to kill by self-MHC I molecules, and that this process is mediated by the interaction of the NK cell inhibitory receptors with their cognate self-MHC I ligands, thereby resulting in NK cell functional competency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NK cells are educated by self-MHC in a manner similar to T cells, but the consequences of this education are different for NK and T cells.
NK cell education is a dynamic process that is not static and is influenced by the local environment, and is thus subject to change.
NK cells are educated in the thymus and the bone marrow, and that NK cells that fail to be licensed by self-MIC class I molecules become functionally impaired.
